knowledge.title_en: Stock-Bond Correlation: When the Hedge Breaks
knowledge.body_en:
For most of the 2000s and 2010s Treasuries rallied when stocks fell, so a 60/40 portfolio hedged itself. That relationship depends on what drives the selloff: growth scares push yields down and bond prices up while stocks fall, but inflation or supply shocks push yields up and equity multiples down at the same time.

When the correlation turns positive, both legs lose at once. Risk-parity and volatility-targeting funds then cut exposure mechanically, selling bonds and stocks into weakness. That forced deleveraging is the 'vicious loop' traders describe: higher yields compress valuations, which triggers more selling of both.
knowledge.why_en: This week the 10-year yield rose 7% while the S&P 500 fell 1.5%, the positive-correlation regime in action.
